items.abstract: <jats:p>With the growing risks involved in surfing the web, the ability to protect users from malicious web content has become essential for combatting cybersecurity threats. Extensive studies have shown the correlation between certain personal-traits and user behavior in the context of cybersecurity. Moreover, recent studies showed that it is possible to predict long-term probability of cyber-attack victimization by analyzing a user's browsing and file-downloading history. However, such prediction models often rely on storing and analyzing personal information such as detailed browsing history, the topics and types of sites the user visited, and even physical location history, hence, potentially compromising user privacy. We developed a simple Markovian model that provides real-time predictions of exposure to malicious web pages by identifying behavioral patterns, as manifested in web-browsing dynamics. Utilizing the Markov chain framework, we extracted a small number of features that serve as proxies to the user's current risk level. Our model was tested on a dataset of web-browsing logs collected over three months, including more than 6 million browsing sessions. Using a logistic regression classifier to predict next-step exposure and exposure further into the session, our model allows for proactive intervention to protect from potential cyber-threats while maintaining user privacy.</jats:p>
